title: Exploration and Insights on Topology Adjustment of Giant Heterometallic Cages Featuring Inorganic Skeletons Assisted by Machine Learning

material_class.structural_family: Oxalate-assisted n × m × l inorganic-skeleton cage

synthesis.procedure: Obtained in a one-pot, high-throughput exploration combining La(NO3)3, [Ni(IDA)], NaOH, and oxalic acid solutions. The La(NO3)3 solution was fixed at 1 mL (0.5 M); the other solution amounts varied among experimental recipes. The mixtures were heated at 80 °C for 3 days, producing shape-distinguishable cluster crystals. The main article does not identify a complete compound-specific recipe.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Shape-distinguishable crystals were obtained; further work-up was not specified in the main article.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A 5 × 5 × 3 parallelepiped cage with eight {LaNi3} vertices and twelve linear linkers: four short {La3Ni2} linkers and eight long linkers. Additional La ions connect the vertices and linkers and occupy interior positions. The reported La74Ni104 nuclearity describes the cage core; the formula also lists four Ni outside its bracketed core.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A 5 × 5 × 5 parallelepiped cage in which all twelve edges between eight {LaNi3} vertices are long linkers. The article describes it as an extension of La74Ni104 in which its four short linkers are replaced by long linkers; additional La ions support the framework and occupy its interior.
